```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Rare-disease registries, cohorts and surveillance systems code diagnoses
with ORPHAcodes, the identifiers of the Orphanet nomenclature. The
nomenclature is revised every year: entities are created, deprecated and
merged, names change, and the classification moves. `orphacodes` makes
that nomenclature a versioned, queryable object in R and provides the
operations a registry needs around it: validation of codes,
standardisation of free-text diagnoses, mapping to ICD-10, ICD-11, OMIM
and other systems, navigation of the classification, update of a
registry to a newer release, and aggregation of cases at the right
level.

```{r setup}
library(orphacodes)
```

## The database

Everything works on an `orphadb` object. `orphafetch()` downloads one
yearly release of the Orphanet nomenclature files for coding (and,
optionally, the Orphadata products for prevalence, genes and the non-ICD
alignments), parses it once and caches it:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
db <- orphafetch("2025")      # a pinned release
db <- orphafetch()            # the current files
orphaversions()               # releases available
```

The package ships `orphamini`, a subset of the 2026 release restricted
to three classifications (rare cardiac diseases, rare neurological
diseases and rare inborn errors of metabolism), which this vignette
uses. Functions tell you once when a code falls outside the subset.
`orphause()` registers a database as the default so that `db` can be
omitted in every call.

```{r}
orphause(orphamini)
orphamini
```

## Look up, search, validate

Codes are accepted in every common format (`"ORPHA:324"`, `"orpha 324"`,
`324`):

```{r}
orphalookup(c("ORPHA:324", "orpha 558", 97929))[, c("orphacode", "name", "status", "level", "aggregation_code")]
orphasearch("cardiomyopathy", level = "Disorder", max = 5)
```

Validation reports the format, presence and status of each code and the
replacement recorded by Orphanet for deprecated codes:

```{r}
orphavalidate(c("ORPHA:324", "166068", "abc", NA, "1"))[, c("input", "issue", "name", "replacement", "relation")]
```

## Standardise free-text diagnoses

`orphastandardize()` matches names on the preferred term, then on
synonyms, then approximately. Ties are reported as ambiguous rather than
resolved silently.

```{r}
reg <- data.frame(dx = c("Fabry disease", "Anderson-Fabry disease", "Fabry desease", "Flu"))
orphastandardize(reg, disease = "dx")
```

## Hierarchy

The Orphanet classification is a polyhierarchy. The package exposes
direct and transitive relations, and three ways to roll a code up to a
single group: the EU aggregation level (subtypes to their disorder), the
preferential parent (head of the linearised classification, no double
counting), or the root of each classification an entity belongs to.

```{r}
orphaancestors("324")[, c("related", "related_name", "depth")]
orphagroup(c("324", "558"), level = "specialty")[, c("orphacode", "group", "group_name")]
```

## Interoperability

Mappings are many-to-many and carry their relation type: `E` exact,
`NTBT` the ORPHAcode is narrower than the target, `BTNT` broader, `ND`
not decided. Nothing is collapsed unless you ask with `best = TRUE`.

```{r}
orphamap("324", to = "ICD10")[, c("orphacode", "code", "relation", "icd_relation", "validation")]
orphafrom("E75.2", from = "ICD10")[, c("orphacode", "name", "relation")]
orphasources()
```

## Versions

`orphahistory()` shows what Orphanet did with a code, `orphaupdate()`
applies the mandatory "Moved to" replacements, following chains, and
`orphadiff()` compares two releases:

```{r}
orphaupdate(c("166068", "324"))
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
d <- orphadiff(orphafetch("2024"), orphafetch("2025"))
d
```

Run on the real 2024 and 2025 releases (11,023 and 11,239 entities)
the summary reads:

```
Orphanet nomenclature 2024 -> 2025
11023 -> 11239 entities
* 216 added
* 0 removed
* 418 renamed
* 60 status changes
* 32 level changes
* 70 preferential parent changes
```

and `d$status` shows where the 60 status changes went: 22 entities
became obsolete, 21 deprecated (with a "Moved to" replacement), 6 were
flagged historic, and 6 inactive entities were reactivated. Orphanet
never removes a code, which is why `removed` is empty; a registry that
pins its release and runs `orphadiff()` at each upgrade sees exactly
what its coded data are exposed to.

### Other languages

`orphafetch(lang = "fr")` fetches the French nomenclature; Czech,
German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish and Portuguese are available
too. Status, level, type and relation labels are decoded from the
Orphanet identifiers, so every function behaves identically whatever
the language; only names and synonyms are localised.

## A registry extract

`orphademo` is a simulated registry extract with the defects met in
practice: synonyms and typos in the diagnosis text, codes written with
prefixes, deprecated and group-level codes, missing values and a
duplicated identifier.

```{r}
head(orphademo)
qc <- orphaqc(orphademo, code = "diagnosis_code", id = "patient_id")
summary(qc)
```

`orphaharmonize()` normalises the codes, applies the replacements,
recovers codes from the diagnosis text when the code is missing or
invalid, and adds the roll-up columns:

```{r}
h <- orphaharmonize(orphademo, code = "diagnosis_code", disease = "diagnosis")
basetable::count(h, "orphacode_source")
```

## Counting and reference prevalence

```{r}
orphaaggregate(h, code = "orphacode", level = "specialty", by = "sex")
```

`orphaprevref()` returns the point prevalence class Orphanet publishes
for each code, preferring a European estimate and falling back to a
worldwide one:

```{r}
a <- orphaaggregate(h, code = "orphacode", level = "disorder")
r <- orphaprevref(head(a$group[!is.na(a$group)], 5))
r[, c("orphacode", "name", "class", "geographic")]
```

## Data capture

`orphachoices()` builds a coded value list for any form or database
constraint; `orpharedcap()` formats it as a REDCap data dictionary row
(an autocomplete dropdown) ready for import.

```{r}
head(orphachoices(), 3)
dd <- orpharedcap(field = "rare_disease", form = "diagnosis")
substr(dd[["Choices, Calculations, OR Slider Labels"]], 1, 80)
```

## Citing Orphanet

The data are published by Orphanet under CC-BY-4.0. `orphacite()` gives
the citation strings and the version used.

```{r}
orphacite()
```
